title: Oncall Contextual Bundle Assembler: automated trace+metrics snapshots for PD/Slack alerts
creator: Marisol Vega
description:
Problem: Oncall responders currently spend significant time gathering context when a critical alert fires: tracing spans, recent error logs, latency heatmaps, and recent deployment metadata. This increases MTTR and creates inconsistency in post-incident artifacts.

Goal: Build a server-side "Contextual Bundle Assembler" that automatically collects a compact evidence bundle whenever a high-severity PagerDuty incident or Slack escalation is created. The bundle should include a 60s condensed trace (top N spans), a 5-minute log/error sample, key metric snapshots (p50/p95/p99 for the affected route), recent deploy commit & model version, and a link to an auto-created postmortem stub. Bundles should be attachable to PD incidents, inserted into Slack incident threads, and stored in the incident artifact store for later audits and QA.

Non-goals: We are not replacing full-fidelity trace retrieval or building a full correlation UI. This is a lightweight compact evidence product to accelerate triage and seed postmortems.
acceptance_criteria: When PD incident with severity=critical/open is created, a Contextual Bundle is assembled within 30s and attached to the PD incident as a file/link
When a Slack escalation message is created in #oncall-escalations, the bundle is posted as the initial thread reply with a brief human-friendly summary
Bundle size should be <= 200KB (compressed) for typical incidents to avoid PD attachment limits
Bundle must include: condensed trace (top N spans), 5m log sample with error exemplars, p50/p95/p99 delta graphs for affected route, deploy metadata (commit, model id), and a postmortem stub link
Automated postmortem stub is created in the postmortem dashboard with incident metadata and a link to the bundle
Feature respects RBAC and audit logging; only users with incident access can download bundles
End-to-end tests cover PD webhook -> assembler -> PD attachment and Slack path; canary rollout shows no more than 0.1% error increase in alert handling latency
design_notes: Event sourcing: listen to incident creation webhook events from PagerDuty and Slack escalation webhook events. Normalize to an internal IncidentEvent schema before assembling bundles.

Trace sampling heuristic: query recent traces by span name and service, score by error/latency impact, and use an importance-ranked top-N algorithm to produce a condensed trace with inferred root cause candidates.

Cost/tradeoff: full trace download is expensive. We'll implement a trace summarizer that fetches only key spans and sibling context. If summarizer fails (timeout/rate limit), fall back to a short trace link only.

Attachment storage: upload bundle artifacts to the incident artifacts S3 bucket with short-lived pre-signed URLs. PD attachments will reference the URL rather than embedding large blobs when possible.
Rate-limiting: introduce an assembly queue with prioritized concurrency. PD alerts are high priority; bulk alerts (alert storms) will be sampled to avoid overload.

Security: bundle generation will call KMS to redact PII fields from logs and will include an audit event for each generated bundle. Ensure private deploy model references are redacted unless requester has access.
User experience: Slack message should include a 2-3 line plain English summary (why this fired, top evidence) plus a link to open the bundle in Console.
Postmortem stub: pre-populate template fields (summary, timeline stub with trace snippet, initial impact estimate) and set status to 'draft'.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (MVP - 2 weeks): implement PD and Slack webhook listeners; basic assembler that pulls traces/logs/metrics; upload bundles to artifacts bucket; attach link to PD incident and post to Slack thread.
Phase 2 (hardening - 3 weeks): add compact trace summarizer, redaction/KMS integration, RBAC checks, and autosampling for alert storms.
Phase 3 (ops & observability - 1 week): dashboards for bundle assembly latency/errors, audit log forwarding, SLOs for assembly time, and runbook link templating.
Phase 4 (rollout - 1 week): canary to 10% of PD services, monitor error/latency impact, expand to all after 72h with no regressions.

Implementation tasks: webhook adapters (ENG-99877), summarizer service (ENG-99880), artifact uploader (ENG-99881), PD attachment integration (ENG-99883), Slack thread poster (ENG-99884), RBAC/audit hooks (ENG-99890), postmortem-stub creator (ENG-99895).
comments: 2026-02-28 - Marisol Vega: Initial triage and spec drafting. Spoke with oncall rotation leads; they validated the 60s condensed trace requirement.
2026-03-03 - Jonah Patel: Design review completed. Decided to prefer pre-signed URLs instead of embedding to avoid PD size limits. Added KMS redaction scope.
2026-03-05 - Lina Chu (SRE): Raised concern about PD API rate limits during alert storms. Proposed adding an assembly queue and sampling policy.
2026-03-07 - Jonah Patel: Implemented webhook listener prototype and wired basic artifact uploader. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/observability/pull/4122
2026-03-09 - QA: Integration tests failing intermittently when trace summarizer times out. Investigating fallback behavior and adding retries with backoff.

2026-03-10 - Marisol Vega: Decided to cap bundle assembly time to 30s. If summarizer exceeds 8s, assembler will include a summary note and the link to full trace instead of blocking attachment. Updated acceptance criteria accordingly.
